I'm confident this is a code issue and the runbook calls for an auto-fix, so I'm leaning toward deciding auto-fix and briefing the coder. The coder isn't among the agents I'm allowed to ask, though, so I'm weighing whether to record an auto-fix decision with a reason and let the dispatch happen elsewhere.

The runbook says auto-fix, so I'm settling on an auto-fix decision, leaving the coder to carry out the fix. I'll also keep the GetDiscountLabel side note in mind and check that the fix won't change totals on valid-code orders.

arguments.reason: The investigator found, with high confidence, that OrderApi.GetOrderTotal (src/OrderService/Api/OrderTotal.cs, line 18) indexes the discount table directly, so the retired code SUMMER25 on order 1003 throws KeyNotFoundException and blocks checkout. The runbook lists this exception as auto-fixable, with the expected behaviour of no discount (total = subtotal), and the fix should leave WELCOME10, VIP20 and no-code totals unchanged. The coder should use a TryGetValue fallback to the subtotal and keep the existing tests passing; the separate GetDiscountLabel quirk for SUMMER25 is noted for the reviewer, not part of this fix.
